title: Development of dermal targeting formulations for squamous cell carcinoma
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because we aim at materializing a new treatment and
preventive modality for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Therefore, the proposed research is relevant to the
NIH’s mission of supporting research into the cause, treatment, and prevention of cancer and skin diseases.

title: 2026 Enzymes, Coenzymes and Metabolic Pathways GRC and GRS
text:
Enzymes drive metabolic processes and complex chemical reactions, acting as the engines of life and powering
the essential chemical reactions that keep our bodies healthy. When these engines malfunction, it can lead to
serious illnesses, yet we still have much to learn about how they operate inside our cells. This project supports
a premier gathering of researchers dedicated to solving these mysteries, with the ultimate goal of engineering
new enzymes and medications to cure disease and enhance human well-being.

title: Project-2: Modeling TE birth defects in animals
text: PROJECT 2 | PROJECT SUMMARY Failure to separate the fetal foregut into distinct trachea and esophagus (TE) can result in a spectrum of life- threatening tracheoesophageal defects (TEDs). The genetic etiology of TEDs is poorly understood, and risk variants are known in only 12% of TED patients. Even in cases where the causative mutations are known such as in developmental transcription factors (TFs), how they result in TEDs is unclear because up until recently the mechanisms of TE morphogenesis were ill defined. We made significant progress in the previous award. Using a combination of Xenopus and mouse embryology, we elucidated the conserved cellular events driving TE morphogenesis and showed that disrupting any step can result in TED-like phenotypes. We used Xenopus CRISPR screens to validate potential TED-causing variants from patient genome sequences. One major discovery was that downstream of Hedgehog (HH) signaling and developmental TFs, endosome-mediated membrane remodeling is required to separate the foregut into distinct TE tubes. Consistent with this, genome sequencing of 185 TED patients from Project 1 revealed an enrichment of damaging variants in membrane/vesicular trafficking genes including the endocytic adaptor ITSN1, which in preliminary data we demonstrated is required for Xenopus TE morphogenesis. The goal of the CLEAR consortium Project 2 is to define the developmental basis of TED with cellular resolution in animal models. We will: Determine the mechanism by which endosome trafficking regulates TE morphogenesis (Aim1). Test the hypothesis that developmental TFs control the cell-specific expression of effector proteins such as endosome trafficking machinery or cargo (Aim2, in collaboration with Project 3). Assess the pathogenicity of patient variants in animals testing the provocative hypothesis that endosomeopathies might be a major cause of TEDs (Aim3).

title: Unravel a novel metabolic pathway orchestrating prostate cancer progression and therapeutic resistance
text:
Prostate cancer stem cells (PCSCs) constitute prostate initiation, progression, metastasis as well 
as drug resistance, leading to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), which 
represents a highly aggressive cancer with poor outcome due to the lack of an effectively 
targeting strategy. Our study aims to identify novel druggable targets critical for maintaining 
PCSCs and CRPC progression in order to develop an effectively therapeutic strategy to target 
PCSC-mediated CRPC progression and drug resistance. Our study will not only reveal a paradigm-shift 
concept and novel mechanistic insight for PCSC regulation, but also offer a highly effective 
strategy for targeting CRPC.

title: Training in Advanced Statistical Methods in Neuroimaging and Genetics
text: To directly address the need to better prepare the scientific workforce for biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research, this program will continue to teach advanced statistical methods. This is the “Training in Advanced Statistical Methods in Neuroimaging and Genetics” course (also known as NeuroStats BootCamp). To meet the needs of the changing landscape, the course content will evolve during this next 5 years from the original content.

title: Algorithm-enabled Patients Activated in Cancer care through Teams (A-PACT) toimprove goals of care communication for people with cancer
text:
Our objective is to improve education and engagement in goals of care communication for high-risk patients
with cancer, in order to reduce care utilization and improve patient-reported mood and communication
regarding care preferences. Through a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study conducted through
NCI's SWOG Cancer Research Network and implemented in NCI's National Community Oncology Research
Program, we will evaluate the effectiveness of a scalable approach combining automated machine learning-
driven patient identification with lay health worker-led engagement in goals of care communication. We will
also identify patient, caregiver, clinician, and organizational characteristics affecting effectiveness and
implementation outcomes, in order to facilitate broad adoption.

title: 1 mm resolution single-photon spectral imaging of the brain
text:
This proposed research project will integrate the disruptive high-performance 3D CZT imaging-spectrometer
technologies with a novel synthetic compound eye (SCE) camera design, as well as an innovative iterative image
reconstruction method using deep-learning based priors, to develop a next-generation clinical brain SPECT
imaging system with transformative spatial resolution and imaging sensitivity unattainable previously. The long-
term objective is to apply this innovative imaging system to human brain SPECT studies using a collection of
various SPECT radiotracers, and develop and advance physiological parametric imaging methodologies, in order
to investigate the long-standing issues in neurobiology and improve our understanding of the interplay and
relationship among cerebral blood flow and perfusion, brain tissue oxygenation, neuronal cell metabolism, and
brain cell tracking under different cognitive challenges and biophysical conditions in healthy and in disease. We
would envision the proposed system to serve as a unique imaging platform to significantly advance our
understanding of neural cell biology and regional brain functions in response to various cognitive, behavioral,
and physiological challenges by employing these unprecedentedly innovative SPECT imaging methodologies in
order to assess all relevant quantitative physiological measurements that will be interpreted in an integrated
fashion and synergistically so that new perspectives in brain research unattainable previously can be formulated.

title: Indiana University Melvin and Bren Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center Support Grant
text: The Indiana University Melvin and Bren Simon Cancer Center is an NCI-designated Cancer Center whose mission is to create an expanding community of researchers and health professionals who conduct outstanding translational research, provide excellence in education, and deliver high quality patient-centered care. We will foster and promote an environment that supports excellence and broad participation as we contribute to the prevention and cure of cancer in Indiana. We recognize that health challenges vary across populations, and we further our mission by drawing on the broad range of perspectives and experiences represented across Indiana.

title: Soft, Morphable, Three?Dimensional Electronic and Microfluidic Micro?Lab for Drug Screening in Engineered Tissues
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it focuses on developing new
technologies for drug discovery and drug development. This study will yield a soft, morphable
electronic and microfluidic hybrid micro-lab for drug screening in mature organoids, and real-time
monitoring of the response of cells and tissues to the delivered drugs.

title: A multidisciplinary approach to study ecotypes driving transmission and pathogenesis of Visceral Leishmaniasis (VL) and Post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) in Eastern Africa
text:
Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a neglected tropical disease which is fatal if left untreated. Majority of VL cases in
the world are reported from Eastern Africa, particularly Ethiopia, Sudan, and Kenya. The goal of this project is to
study the risk factors that are associated with transmission of this infection in these high endemic countries,
understand the ecology and behavior of sand flies which transmit this disease and identify potential host and
parasite factors responsible for disease progression and pathogenesis. These studies will provide critical data
required for developing control and prevention strategies for elimination of VL from Eastern Africa.

title: Defining Therapeutically Targetable Regulators of Tumor-Intrinsic Immune Suppression in Glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM), a common and highly aggressive brain cancer with a universally fatal prognosis, is
characterized by a vast degree of heterogeneity and an immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment
influenced by spatial architecture and distinct cellular phenotypes. The work we propose will robustly define
regions of localized immune-suppression in GBM and unearth the cellular mechanisms integral to these
regions that are involved in modulating the anti-tumor immune response. Favorable results from this
proposal will provide a rationale for combining therapeutics targeting genetic regulators of
immunosuppressive cell states with other immunotherapies to treat GBM.

title: Integrating Single-Cell TCR Landscapes and Structural Fingerprints to Advance Leukemia Immunotherapies
text:
The unique complexities of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and its immune micro-environment have greatly
impaired efforts on the development of effective T-cell-based therapies for these malignancies. Major factors
contributing to this problem relate to the limitations of the computational tools used to guide the identiﬁcation of
leukemia-speciﬁc peptide-targets and therapeutic T-cell receptors (TCRs). To address this problem, we propose
deploying cutting-edge structural modeling and molecular ﬁngerprinting methods to the largest available single-
cell TCR sequencing dataset of AML patients, therefore enabling AI-driven design of novel and safer T-cell-based
immunotherapies for AML and other leukemias.

title: Sea star oocytes as a model system for Wnt pathway activation through novel signaling organelles
text:
Communication between different types of cells is essential for human development, and when it goes wrong,
this can lead to birth defects and cancer. In this work, we are defining how a protein called Dishevelled, and
filamentous cellular structures, mediate a particular type of cellular communication important for many aspects
of human development and disease.

title: The Genetic Epidemiology of Radiation-Associated Contralateral Breast Cancer
text:
There is an acute need to identify women at significant risk of developing contralateral breast cancer (CBC) after
a primary breast cancer diagnosis, and the subset of women who may be especially sensitive to radiation-
associated second cancers. Despite major advances in identifying breast cancer susceptibility genes, the role of
inherited genetics in modulating risk of CBC in women exposed to radiation therapy, a potent carcinogen,
remains poorly understood which has limited the ability of providers and patients to select tailored treatment
and/or surveillance plans. The proposed study seeks to identify the genetic determinants of radiation-associated
breast cancer and develop detailed CBC risk estimation, with the long-term goal of enabling informed therapeutic
decisions that balance benefits and risks to optimize outcomes.

title: A Toolkit for Analysis and Visualization of Preclinical Rodent Neuroimaging Experiments
text:
Relevance to Public Health
This project will develop an open source suite of software for the processing, analysis, and visualization of rodent
brain imaging data, which will enhance the ability of neuroscience researchers to perform preclinical studies on
rodent models. This software will provide advanced capabilities for analyzing multimodal imaging data, including
imagery from magnetic resonance imaging and optical microscopy studies, with the goal of improving
understanding of processes and mechanisms underlying neurological diseases and disorders and their potential
treatment. The software will include interactive processing to facilitate ease of use, as well as command line
tools to enable large scale processing for larger studies.

title: Gain-of-function MRGPRX2 mutations in drug induced hypersensitivity reactions
text:
Adverse reactions to therapeutic drugs have been increasing in recent years but the mechanisms remain
unknown. We hypothesize that gain-of-function mutations in a cell surface receptor expressed in mast cells
contribute to these reactions. We will develop humanized mouse models expressing mutated receptors in mast
cells, which will provide new preclinical models to study genetic modifications that are involved in adverse drug
reactions.

title: Epigenomic and Immune Phenotypes integration with Systems Biology
text: CORE B PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT The Epigenomics and Systems Data Integration (Core B) will serve the goals of the WE-CAIR Program to understand the impact of wildfire smoke exposure, particularly fine particulate material (PM2.5), on human health. Core B will provide essential services to the projects that include the generation, analysis, and integration of DNA methylation data from candidate genes and genome- wide sequencing approaches. The significance of Core B analyses lies in recognizing interindividual differences in health outcomes, influenced by genetic factors and social determinants. Core B will serve Projects 1-4 by generating and analyzing epigenomic and immune signatures of wildfire smoke exposure and how these patterns relate to immune, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems. Core B will employ both candidate gene- and discovery-based approaches, including whole genome bisulfite sequencing and machine learning, to identify biomarkers across different tissues and two species. Specifically, Aim 1 will generate epigenetic data from mouse and human samples to serve Projects 1- 4. Aim 2 will perform bioinformatic analyses to deliver back to Projects 1-4 lists of differentially methylated genes and correlated methylated gene networks from both bulk WGBS of each tissue (lung, heart, blood, and brain) and single cell methylomes of specific cell types of interest, including ILC2s (Project 1) and airway epithelial cells (Project 3). Aim 3 will support Projects 1-4 in integrating DNA methylation signatures of wildfire smoke at the intersection of psychosocial stress, demographic, experimental, immune, behavioral and clinical outcome variables across two species (Projects 1-4). Based on the epigenetic, immune, and behavioral data, Core B will identify the WE-CAIR “resilience” (healthy) vs. “high-susceptibility” wildfire smoke respiratory signatures of epigenetic and clinical predictors from the COPD patient and control cohorts together with Cores A and D. This comprehensive approach integrates molecular, immune, and behavioral data across different species, aiming to contribute novel insights into the health consequences of wildfire smoke exposure for each of the research projects within WE-CAIR.

title: RNA 3D structurome reconstruction and characterization
text:
Project Narrative / Relevance to Public Health
RNA structure makes significant impact on the fate and function of RNAs. This research program will develop
and apply statistical method to reconstruct and characterize RNA 3D structure for all RNAs using high-throughput
RNA-RNA spatial interaction data. Completion of the project will provide novel insights on the relationship of RNA
structure and human diseases, enabling targeted identification and improvement of potential targets for disease
diagnosis and treatment.

title: Impact of T cell receptor signaling on memory CD8+ T cell stemness
text:
CD8+ T cells regulate the adaptive response to infection, antitumor immunity, and autoimmunity through
their remarkable ability to detect intracellular antigen and mediate potent cytotoxic functions. Further
investigating mechanisms by which long-lasting immunological memory is generated remains of great
significance to human health. Findings from this study will enhance our understanding of how the quality of T
cell receptor signaling imprints a memory program in CD8+ T cells with important implications in the rational
design of vaccine development and adoptive T cell transfer immunotherapies.

title: Image-based Detection and Spatial Monitoring of Secondary Lymphedema in Head and Neck Cancer
text:
Secondary lymphedema (LD), a disease with no known cure, is one of the most significant survivorship
morbidities in head and neck cancer. The primary way to diagnose LD is a physical evaluation, which is
not standardized. This project develops a first-in-class, low-cost, convenient, automated and objective
LD detection and measurement approach through a combination of learning-free spatial algorithms
and smartphone instrumentation.
